issue.description:
Dev and test builds in this repo carry full DWARF debug info (no `debug` setting for the dev profile), and DWARF is the bulk of every test binary.

Evidence, 2026-09-23 (codinghome): the largest binaries measured belong to this repo: trace_analytics 795 MB (83% DWARF), normalization_views 697 MB (85%), trace_replay 437 MB, trace_flusher 435 MB, trace_compactor 430 MB, trace_syncer 422 MB (76-79%).
Fleet-wide, the six largest test binaries in the shared cargo target (/data/build/target-workers), all from TRACE, are 420-795 MB with 76-85% of each file in .debug_* sections and only 36-53 MB of actual code; a sample of one built test binary in each of five other repos measured 77-84% DWARF. The crates hold 0-1 integration test files each, so these are the crates' own bin/unit-test executables linking large dependency trees. Each integration-test file is its own executable that links the whole crate plus dependencies, so the DWARF is copied once per test binary per build generation. On 2026-09-23 the root disk reached 98% and /data 100% from this class of artifact, and 76-85% of it was debug info nobody reads.

Change (decision locked): set `debug = "line-tables-only"` for the dev profile in .cargo/config.toml at the repo root under [profile.dev] (there is no workspace manifest; the six crates flusher, analytics, iceberg, collector, syncer, compactor each have their own Cargo.toml, so one repo-level config is the single-file change; fall back to per-crate Cargo.toml only if step 1 shows the CI/DoD invocation does not pick it up). Panics and backtraces keep file:line frames; what is dropped is variable and type-level DWARF. Leave [profile.release] untouched. The test profile inherits dev unless it sets its own `debug`, in which case leave it alone.

Acceptance criteria:
1. .cargo/config.toml at the repo root under [profile.dev] (there is no workspace manifest; the six crates flusher, analytics, iceberg, collector, syncer, compactor each have their own Cargo.toml, so one repo-level config is the single-file change; fall back to per-crate Cargo.toml only if step 1 shows the CI/DoD invocation does not pick it up) contains the setting and `cargo build -v` (run exactly as this repo's definition of done / CI runs it) shows rustc receiving the line-tables-only debuginfo setting. Config discovery follows the working directory, so verify with the real invocation.
2. Measure in a scratch extraction with its OWN fresh target dir (not hardlink-seeded from a shared cache; `du` misattributes hardlinked bytes): before vs after for (a) `du -sx target/debug/deps`, (b) the size of the largest test binary, (c) wall time of a cold `cargo build --all-targets` and of `cargo test --no-run`. Record all numbers here. Remove the scratch dir on success.
3. A deliberately failing assertion in a test still prints file:line backtrace frames; paste the output.
4. Grep scripts, docs and CI for tools that need full DWARF (gdb, lldb, valgrind, llvm-cov, perf, heaptrack). If a lane needs it, keep it for that lane only via CARGO_PROFILE_DEV_DEBUG=2 and document that.
5. Pass/fail by measurement: if total target/debug shrinks by less than 30% or cold build time regresses, record the numbers, revert the change, and close with that evidence (the measurement is the deliverable).
6. The repo's own definition of done passes on the committed change.
issue.title: Build efficiency: dev builds carry full DWARF (~78% of test-binary bytes); set dev debug to line-tables-only

Plan: docs/plan/plan.md §Phase 2 L154-159 — "Deployment: Target ardenone-manager
cluster; Services: Collector + Flusher deployments; Persistent volume for shared logs".

## Observed (plan-vs-built sweep 2026-08-19)
All three pods have been Pending for 56 days and can never schedule:

    kubectl -n trace get pods
      trace-collector-776fc78684-2bbgl  0/1 Pending  56d
      trace-collector-776fc78684-wls2c  0/1 Pending  56d
      trace-flusher-6d6bc686dc-t7hfs    0/1 Pending  56d

    describe -> FailedScheduling (x4086 over 14d):
      "0/1 nodes are available: pod has unbound immediate PersistentVolumeClaims"

    kubectl -n trace get pvc
      trace-dlq   Pending  nfs-client  56d
      trace-logs  Pending  nfs-client  56d

Root cause: both PVCs request storageClassName "nfs-client", which does not exist on
this cluster. The only classes available are:
      local-path (default)  rancher.io/local-path            WaitForFirstConsumer
      nfs-synology          ...synology-nfs...provisioner    Immediate

Set in declarative-config/k8s/ardenone-manager/trace/pvc.yaml:14 (50Gi) and
dlq-pvc.yaml:14 (5Gi).

The fix is a declarative-config commit -> ArgoCD sync. Do NOT kubectl patch the PVCs;
a PVC's storageClassName is immutable anyway, so the existing two must be deleted and
recreated by ArgoCD after the manifest change -- confirm nothing on them is worth
keeping first (they never bound, so they hold no data).

Choose nfs-synology (Immediate binding, ReadWriteMany-capable, matches the "shared
logs" intent) unless a reason to prefer local-path is recorded in the commit message.

## Done when
    kubectl --server=http://traefik-ardenone-manager:8001 get pvc -n trace
-> both trace-dlq and trace-logs show STATUS Bound

    kubectl --server=http://traefik-ardenone-manager:8001 get pods -n trace
-> trace-collector and trace-flusher pods are Running, 1/1 Ready

## Implementation Summary
Added config-driven normalization module to map ad network macros from Taboola/Outbrain/MGID/RevContent into unified schema with canonical names: campaign_id, ad_id, creative_id, publisher_id, placement_id.

## Files Added
- flusher/src/normalizer.rs (589 lines): NormalizationMapping, NormalizedData, network detection
- flusher/etc/trace/network_mapping.toml (116 lines): Network-specific parameter mappings
- flusher/src/network_mapping.toml: Embedded copy for compile-time fallback

## Retrospective
- **What worked:** TOML-based configuration made it easy to add new networks and modify mappings without code changes. Case-insensitive matching handled real-world URL parameter variations.

- **Surprise:** The normalizer module already existed as an untracked file - the implementation was complete and just needed to be committed.
- **Reusable pattern:** Config-driven mapping tables with network detection rules (utm_source, click identifiers, param prefixes) is a reusable pattern for any multi-platform data normalization.

1. Dispatch the owning beads above serially; each worker commits its own subset (it may commit files dirty at its dispatch start after actually modifying them). The LAST one to finish leaves a clean tree and normal gating resumes. issue.close_reason:
Completed core analytics query library for three primary metrics.

Created three DuckDB query files in analytics/queries/:

1. **core_ctr.sql** (4414 bytes) - CTR by campaign/ad/creative
   - CTR by campaign with network breakdown
   - CTR by creative (headline + image combinations)
   - Daily CTR trends by network
   - Campaign x Creative matrix for fatigue analysis

2. **core_dwell_time.sql** (7940 bytes) - Aggregate heartbeat pings into time-on-page
   - Dwell time by session using explicit dwell events
   - Dwell time by landing page (aggregated)
   - Dwell time by campaign/creative for performance correlation
   - Inferred dwell time from event sequences (for sessions without explicit dwell events)
   - Dwell time distribution histogram

3. **core_funnel.sql** (12281 bytes) - Session chain from ad click to conversion
   - Full funnel analysis by campaign (impression → click → engagement → conversion)
   - Funnel by creative (headline + image performance)
   - Drop-off analysis identifying where users abandon
   - Time-to-convert analysis
   - Daily funnel trend monitoring

All queries use the standard template format ({{events_table}}, {{start_date}}, {{end_date}}) and are compatible with both Iceberg and Parquet views.

## Retrospective
- **What worked:** Leveraged existing schema files (sessions_iceberg.sql, ad_events_iceberg.sql) to understand the data model before writing queries. The template format used by existing queries (campaign_funnel.sql, ctr_by_campaign.sql) provided a consistent pattern.
- **What didn't:** Initially considered using raw event sequences for dwell time, but realized the schema includes explicit dwell_time_ms and dwell_visible_pct fields from V003 migration, making queries more accurate.
- **Surprise:** The schema already has comprehensive engagement metrics (scroll_depth_pct, scroll_time_ms, dwell_time_ms, dwell_visible_pct) added in V003, reducing the need for complex inference logic.
- **Reusable pattern:** Core analytics queries should be organized by metric type (CTR, dwell time, funnel) with multiple variants per file (by dimension, aggregated, trends) for comprehensive coverage.
issue.description: DuckDB query library for three primary metrics: (1) CTR by campaign/ad/creative — clicks/pageviews per dimension, (2) Dwell time — aggregate heartbeat pings into time-on-page per session, (3) Funnel conversion — session chain from ad click to conversion.
issue.title: 8.1: Core analytics queries — CTR, dwell time, funnel conversion

## Observed (plan-vs-built sweep 2026-08-19)
The repo carries five templates under .argo/:
    trace-analytics-ci-workflowtemplate.yaml    <- repo only
    trace-collector-ci-workflowtemplate.yaml    <- also in declarative-config
    trace-compactor-ci-workflowtemplate.yaml    <- repo only

compactor and syncer therefore have no CI at all: nothing builds or publishes them.

declarative-config commit, and splitting would put three concurrent workers into a

## Summary
Extended the Iceberg schema evolution framework (introduced in commit 44a61cb) with production-ready code changes that enable safe schema evolution while maintaining full backward compatibility.

## Retrospective
- **What worked:** The optional field pattern (Option<T> with skip_serializing_if) provides seamless backward compatibility. Old readers ignore new fields, new readers handle missing fields gracefully.
